summary: Reproduced the paused concurrent disk-weight-update race in the prepared TokenizerManager: the first scheduler response completed the second caller's replacement future and left the first caller pending. Added a dedicated operation lock because scheduler responses have no operation identifier, retained writer-lock ordering for unpaused updates, kept pause state stable during paused updates, and drained an in-flight response before propagating caller cancellation.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before scheduler-boundary reproduction on the unmodified implementation: concurrent paused updates lost the first completion, and cancellation allowed a second update to dispatch before the first response was drained. Sequential and two-worker boundary cases passed. Raw output: reports/j-132bdab73f8f/raw/failing-before.log

Passing-after regression and adjacent coverage: 20 tests passed, including concurrent paused ownership, cancellation and repeated cancellation draining, pause/resume ordering, unpaused RWLock writer preference, cancelled completion metadata publication, sequential updates, multi-worker aggregation, and existing runtime config behavior. Raw output: reports/j-132bdab73f8f/raw/passing-after-final.log
Changed Python sources compile and the patch has no whitespace errors. Raw output: reports/j-132bdab73f8f/raw/static-checks.log

The assigned environment exposes exactly one AMD Instinct MI355X with gfx950 capability through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. This was environment evidence only, not GPU execution. Raw output: reports/j-132bdab73f8f/raw/gpu-environment.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The reproduced defect and regression operate at the TokenizerManager/scheduler-message boundary and perform no tensor or model computation. One assigned MI355X/gfx950 was visible, but running an unrelated GPU smoke would not validate this async ownership bug.

remaining_limitations: No model weights were available or needed, so no full HTTP server or model weight reload was run; the deterministic regression validates the exact untagged scheduler-response boundary described by the issue, not model semantic accuracy.
No multi-node or distributed serving workload was run. The independent two-worker test validates response aggregation in the manager fixture only.
The prepared interpreter did not contain black or ruff modules; compileall, git diff --check, focused tests, and adjacent tests were run locally instead.
